how.intro: Progress here is what you have demonstrated. Each competency has a learner state, and only an evidence record you add changes it.

how.evidence.title: What counts as evidence
how.evidence.intro: The evidence a route asks for depends on its capability type, which the line under the route's title names.
how.evidence.note: Exit evidence shows a competency is {demonstrated}; {transferred}, {retained}, and {applied} each need evidence of their own.
how.steps.title: A route's steps
how.steps.intro: Every route sets its steps in this order and numbers them in its contents. The diagnostic comes first, so you read only what you are missing.
how.review.title: Why reviews come back
how.review.delay: You can demonstrate a competency today and fail to recall it a month later, so the atlas checks again after a delay.
how.review.when: Reviews start once a competency is {demonstrated}. The gap before the next check grows after a successful check and shrinks after a missed one.
how.review.how: A review is a task from the route's diagnostic, answered from memory before you reread anything. A check passed after the delay is the evidence for {retained}.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: What the atlas keeps about you, and what it sends where. There are no analytics and no tracking.
privacy.local.title: In your browser
privacy.local.body: Your progress, evidence records, diagnostic answers, opened-source marks, lab code, decision-lab answers, and the language you last read stay in this browser's local storage. None of it is sent anywhere; exporting progress.yaml saves a copy as a file.
privacy.cookie.title: The one cookie
privacy.cookie.body: The only cookie is the session cookie, set when you sign in. Page scripts cannot read it, and it is sent only to this site over HTTPS. While you sign in it holds a one-time check for up to 10 minutes; after that, a random session ID that expires after 30 days or when you sign out.
privacy.cookie.optional: Signing in is optional: browsing, diagnostics, labs, and progress work without it.
privacy.stored.title: What the server stores
privacy.stored.user: Your user record: an internal ID, the provider you signed in with (GitHub or Google), that provider's ID for your account, your display name, and when the record was created.
privacy.stored.sessions: Your sessions: a hash of each session ID, when it started, and when it expires.
privacy.stored.usage: Usage counters: how many AI requests you made on each day.
privacy.stored.not: Nothing else: not your email address, not the provider's access token, and not your answers, code, or progress.
privacy.sent.title: What is sent where
privacy.sent.signin: Signing in takes you to GitHub or Google, which return your account ID and name to the atlas. Nothing is posted to your account.
privacy.sent.ai: AI help is not available yet. When it is, your answers and code are sent to the model provider only when you use an AI action, and are not stored, except a message you report as wrong.
privacy.sent.host: The site runs on Cloudflare, which handles each request to deliver it.
privacy.delete.title: Removing your data
privacy.delete.body: Signing out deletes the session. To have your user record and usage counters deleted, contact the owner through the links at the bottom of the page.
